Chapter 9: The Broader Human Experience — Society, Justice, and Solidarity
The absurd isn’t just something we wrestle with on our own—it weaves its way into the heart of how we live together, the societies we build, and the values we share.
In a world where there aren’t always clear answers, questions of justice and solidarity matter even more. So, how do we treat each other when there’s no guarantee of fairness, no ultimate reward or punishment waiting at the end?
Picture a community coming together after a disaster. There’s no promise their efforts will pay off, and no one can say for sure that things will improve. But in that moment—when people lend a hand, rebuild side by side—there’s this incredible sense of shared purpose.
The absurd is still there, lingering in the background. But instead of facing it alone, people stand together.
When it comes to justice, the absurd actually makes it a matter of choice. It’s not about blindly following some rulebook handed down from above. It’s about asking ourselves—together—what kind of world do we want to create?
It means recognizing each person’s dignity, even if the universe itself seems indifferent.
Think about a group of workers demanding fair treatment. They probably know the odds are stacked against them, and that success isn’t certain. Still, by standing in solidarity, refusing to accept injustice, they carve out meaning where none has been given. Their unity is a quiet rebellion against the absurd.
Most of us want to believe that justice always wins, that good people get rewarded and bad actors face consequences. But life doesn’t always play out that way, does it?
The real challenge is to keep fighting for justice anyway—to keep caring, to keep building communities built on support and compassion.
Solidarity doesn’t make the absurd go away. But it does make it easier to bear.
It’s a gentle reminder that, even in a world that might not offer ultimate meaning, we can still choose to stand together, to help each other, and to create something better—even if just for a little while.
